Please read /papers/investigations-5/09_green_potentials_newman_flow/notes/02_GNP_CONTINUATION_AND_PROMPTS_20261110.md. Let's begin the sub-investigation 09_green_potentials_newman_flow/01_riemann_siegel_evolution. 

Is the research-overview complete? If not, we should make it more robust, because the last prompt set up the parent folder as well.
I’ll read the continuation note and the repository’s established-results guidance, then check whether the sub-investigation has a complete overview of its own or still relies on the parent setup.

The child overview is a useful starting summary, but it is not yet complete enough to guide the investigation independently. It leaves the normalization, usable parameter ranges, quantitative success test, and several inherited limitations in the parent material. I’ll bring those into the child overview and make the first research decision more precise.

One important gap is now clear: the cited nonzero-time Riemann–Siegel approximation covers the zero strip, while the Green calculation also needs values at heights 4 and 8. The revised overview will make that mismatch explicit and distinguish approximation accuracy from the signed bound the investigation actually needs.
If it is not clear, we want arguments that extend to arbitrary height - so specific heights are only stepping stones. I may be misinterpreting what you said though

That clarifies an important requirement. I’ll make arbitrary height the central objective: bounds must hold for every sufficiently large height, including exceptional locations, with their height dependence explicit. Specific heights can test a method, but won’t count as completing the research task. The revised overview will also distinguish uniformity in height from uniformity as Newman time approaches zero.

I’ve made the arbitrary-height requirement explicit in the overview. The success test now compares the retained value and the complete error with the defect size as height grows. I’m aligning the plan and continuation prompt so future work cannot treat a successful finite-height calculation as the endpoint.

The overview now separates the inherited results from the missing arbitrary-height estimate and spells out the conditions each possible approach would need to meet. I’m finishing the consistency checks and recording the assessment; the first mechanism-selection task remains open.

The original overview was a useful setup summary, but incomplete as a standalone research brief. I’ve expanded the [existing overview](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/09_green_potentials_newman_flow/01_riemann_siegel_evolution/research-overview/01_GNP_RS_RESEARCH_OVERVIEW_20261110.md) and aligned the plan and continuation prompt.

It now explicitly requires:

- Arguments extending to **arbitrary height**, including exceptional centers; specific heights remain stepping stones.
- Precise normalization, time ranges, height dependence and inherited assumptions.
- Quantitative comparison with the defect scale, separating approximation accuracy from the missing signed-value estimate.
- Complete treatment of tails, denominators and collision controls.

It is now a substantive starting brief; the mathematical argument remains open. Source passages and local links were checked.

**Next: [B] GNP-RS-B01 — Astra:** select one formulation and an arbitrary-height estimate to pursue.

Please continue with [B] GNP-RS-B01. 

Track your progress in the research progress folder, write research notes in the notes folder, and record chat history in the chat-histories folder. Please provide guidance for the continuation at the end of your research, and a continuation note for model changes, also mentioning the suggested continuation model in the chat.

I’ll begin GNP-RS-B01 from the revised arbitrary-height brief, record its activation, and test the complete evolved formulas against one quantitative consumer. I’ll save the reasoning, disposition, and model-change handoff as I go.

I’m focusing on a time range that shrinks like \(1/\log X\), so the question remains meaningful as height grows. There may be a useful intermediate step: derive a uniform prime baseline for the Green calculation’s outer boundary and center at these nonzero times. That would isolate the remaining signed logarithmic estimate without assuming it.

The inherited heat-density work already supplies estimates on the wider strip, with Gaussian tails included. I’ll use that to prepare a fixed proof request for the nonzero-time prime baseline. Separately, the known last-block estimate shows why bounding the arithmetic terms by separate magnitudes is inadequate here: its allowance grows with \(\log X\), while the chosen defect margin stays fixed.

B01 now has a concrete direction: the chosen normalization cancels exactly from the Green functional, leaving an outer contribution that looks tractable uniformly at arbitrary height. The remaining signed critical-boundary integral is still open. I’m checking that distinction and preparing the bounded proof request for the next model.

The check confirms the main limitation: the separate-magnitude bound grows like \(\log X\), while the chosen defect margin is fixed. That rules out this particular bound for the selected regime; it says nothing adverse about the actual field. I’m recording B01 as complete at decision scope, with the uniform outer-baseline estimate explicitly left for E01 to prove.

The continuation package now points to **[E] GNP-RS-E01, recommended GPT-6.1 Sol**. It asks for a proof valid at every sufficiently large height in the selected shrinking-time band. I’m checking the source references and saved records so the next model can start from a fixed statement, with the unresolved signed estimate clearly identified.

**B01 is complete at decision and handoff scope.** The selected argument targets every sufficiently large height, with
\[
\lambda=\frac{c}{\log(X/(4\pi))},\qquad \tfrac12\le c\le1.
\]
This approaches time zero as height grows, but does not cover the time-zero slice.

The [research note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/09_green_potentials_newman_flow/01_riemann_siegel_evolution/notes/01_GNP_RS_B01_TRANSITION_SCALE_GREEN_BASELINE_20261111.md) establishes an exact harmonic-normalization identity and shows why the specified separate-magnitude bound fails: its allowance grows like \(\log X\), while the defect margin stays fixed. This does not rule out phase-sensitive estimates.

The proposed uniform outer prime-baseline estimate remains **unproved**. Even proving it would leave the signed critical-boundary estimate open.

Progress, references and the same-assistant assessment are saved. Chat history was refreshed, with final-reply capture arranged.

**Next: [E] GNP-RS-E01 — GPT-6.1 Sol**, to prove that fixed uniform baseline or identify its precise failed step. The [model-change continuation note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/09_green_potentials_newman_flow/01_riemann_siegel_evolution/notes/02_GNP_RS_B01_RETURN_AND_MODEL_CHANGE_20261111.md) links the frozen request and explains the remaining obligations.

Please continue with [E] GNP-RS-E01 using the frozen request. Keep progress, research notes, and chat history updated, and provide continuation guidance and a model-change note with the suggested next model.

I’ll read the frozen E01 request, verify its recorded inputs, and work through the proof within its stated scope. I’ll keep the progress record and chat history current, then leave a continuation note with the result, remaining gap, and suggested next model.

The frozen request and all recorded inputs match. The key estimate is working: on the two outer lines, the heat weights can be removed with an \(O(1/\log X)\) error while retaining the full growing sum. I’m checking the reflected contribution and logarithmic tails next; the critical-boundary integral stays exact.

The four proof steps now fit together. The reflected sum and correction have polynomially small errors, the outer lines have an independent lower bound that permits taking logarithms, and the remote boundary contributes \(O(X^{-3}\log^2 X)\). I’m writing the uniform estimate and its onset conditions; it gives the requested baseline, while the favorable signed-value bound remains open.

The self-check supports E01 as proved from the named inherited inputs, at internal checking scope. The result is \(J=I-P+O(1/\log X)\), uniformly across the requested band. I’m updating the handoff to recommend Astra for the remaining conceptual task: finding an independent, phase-sensitive upper bound for \(I-P\).

The proof, assessment, and next-model note are saved, and the current guidance now points to B02 rather than repeating E01. I’m checking the document links and verifying that the frozen request and earlier mathematical evidence are unchanged. The continuation keeps the same arbitrary-height band and defect margin.

**E01 is complete.** The frozen estimate is proved from the named inherited inputs, with same-assistant internal checking:
\[
|J_\lambda(X)-I_\lambda(X)+P_{c,\lambda}(X)|\le \frac{C_*}{L_X},
\qquad \lambda=\frac c{L_X},\quad c\in[1/2,1].
\]
It holds for **every sufficiently large height**, with finite, analytically specified constants and onset.

The [proof and error accounting](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/09_green_potentials_newman_flow/01_riemann_siegel_evolution/notes/03_GNP_RS_E01_UNIFORM_OUTER_BASELINE_PROOF_20261111.md) cover all four requested groups. The favorable signed upper bound for \(I-P\) remains open; this does not establish zero exclusion or the time-zero endpoint.

Progress and chat history are updated, with final-reply capture arranged.

**Next: [B] GNP-RS-B02 — GPT-6 Astra**, to choose/test an independent phase-sensitive upper estimate for \(I-P\). The [model-change continuation note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/09_green_potentials_newman_flow/01_riemann_siegel_evolution/notes/04_GNP_RS_E01_RETURN_AND_MODEL_CHANGE_20261111.md) gives the precise scope and links the continuation prompt. B02 remains unactivated.

Please continue with [B] GNP-RS-B02 using the continuation note. Keep progress, research notes, and chat history updated, and provide continuation guidance and a model-change note with the suggested next model.

I’ll read the B02 continuation, verify the saved inputs, and test the proposed signed-estimate routes within its bounded scope. I’ll keep the progress record, research notes, and chat history current, then leave continuation guidance with the suggested next model.

I’m comparing two routes: a Jensen bound using the coherent quadratic mean, and a contour comparison with the shifted zeta field. The first has a measurable loss that may already exceed the defect margin. The second must retain the zeros enclosed by the contour; I’m checking whether it yields an estimate beyond another identity.

The E01 inputs match their recorded identities. The quadratic-mean route has a definite obstruction when cross terms are paid as nonnegative costs. I’m separating that proved limitation from the stronger question—whether retaining all those cross terms still leaves Jensen’s inequality too weak—which now has a concrete analytical proof target.

The contour comparison retains a shifted time-zero zero potential and a signed log difference; it does not supply a favorable upper bound by itself. I also checked the earlier correlation-branch Jensen analysis: it provides a related warning, but uses a different observable, so its obstruction cannot simply be imported here.

The two-route comparison is complete. The proved obstruction applies to nonnegative payments for cross terms; the stronger obstruction for the exact coherent moment is still unproved. I’m saving a bounded E03 request for that moment calculation, with an explicit comparison to the defect margin and a stop rule if the proposed proof fails.

The notes and frozen handoff are saved. I’m checking that the overview, progress register and continuation prompt all distinguish the proved payment-class obstruction from the proposed exact-moment result. The next task remains unactivated, and the missing signed logarithmic bound remains open.

The document checks passed across 29 files and 452 local links, and the earlier mathematical inputs and frozen E01 request are unchanged. I’m refreshing the chat archive and arranging capture of the final reply. The continuation recommends E03 / GPT-6.1 Sol for the fixed moment-law proof; it does not treat that result as established.

**B02 is complete at bounded-decision scope**, with same-assistant checking.

The [research note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/09_green_potentials_newman_flow/01_riemann_siegel_evolution/notes/05_GNP_RS_B02_JENSEN_AND_SHIFTED_ZETA_COMPARISON_20261111.md) establishes:

- A Jensen allowance fails at arbitrarily large heights when its moment bound retains the diagonal and pays cross terms and errors nonnegatively.
- The shifted-zeta comparison gives an exact identity, but leaves a coupled signed estimate unpaid.

The stronger obstruction using the **exact coherent moment remains unproved**. No favorable signed upper bound or zero exclusion was obtained.

Progress, notes, references and chat history are updated; final-reply capture is arranged.

**Next: [E] GNP-RS-E03 — GPT-6.1 Sol**, to prove the proposed moment limit and check its scoped Jensen consequence. The [continuation and model-change note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/09_green_potentials_newman_flow/01_riemann_siegel_evolution/notes/06_GNP_RS_B02_RETURN_AND_MODEL_CHANGE_20261111.md) links the frozen request and gives the reading order, limits and continuation prompt.
